correctness.rationale: Rebuilt PG(2,4) independently from F4=F2[x]/(x^2+x+1) logic and re-ran inputs/artifacts/verify.py: ALL CHECKS PASS. F4 arithmetic verified (add=XOR; mul w*w=w2, w2*w2=w, w*w2=1 with w^3=1); canonical nonzero-vector representatives give 21 points/21 line-normals; regularity 5/5 on both sides asserted and passed. KST derivation checked: sum_l C(r_l,2)<=C(8,2)=28 holds because two distinct points span a unique plane line and restriction to L only drops terms; hence sum r_l^2<=56+I and I^2<=8(56+I), i.e. I<=(8+sqrt(1856))/2=25.54, integer <=25. Spectral form checked: 5*64/21+2*8=31.238. Prefix-optimality argument is sound: for fixed P, I(P,L)=sum_{l in L} deg_P(l) is maximized by the top-8 degrees, so one-sided maxima bound all pairs. Degree-sequence lemma verified by exhaustive partition enumeration: exactly two multisets of 8 nonnegative integers summing to 25 have sum-of-squares in [79,81], namely (3^7,4) [sq 79] and (2,3^5,4^2) [sq 81]; no type has sq 80, closing the terse prose around the sq-80 case. Dual enumeration maxima independently re-verified: k=7->21 (360/side), k=8->24 (7560/side), k=9->28 (90720/side), k=10->33 (70560/side), both sides. Attaining-pair total 22680 independently confirmed by DP subset counting (no pair enumeration). Max top-7 degree sum over point 8-sets is 22, so no attaining pair uses a degree-0 line, validating pair_census.py's restriction to deg>=1 candidates (no missed pairs). Explicit witnesses in DRAFT section 4 match pair_census.json coordinates and verify to I=24 with the claimed types. One presentation typo found and corrected in RESULT.md: DRAFT line 121 writes full-21 profile (4,3^7,2^4,1^10) which has 22 entries summing to 43; the artifact (pair_census.json) correctly has (4,3^6,2^4,1^10) (21 entries, sum 40=8*5). The theorem, pair-type census, and evidence are unaffected. Final 25-exclusion rests on finite enumeration (disclosed), not a synthetic elimination; proof vs computation is properly distinguished.

originality.rationale: Nearest priors fetched and compared substantively: arXiv:0711.4427 (Vinh finite-field Szemeredi-Trotter/sum-product, asymptotic), arXiv:1609.06284 (Stevens-de Zeeuw O(m^11/15 n^11/15) arbitrary-field bound, asymptotic with characteristic constraint), arXiv:2303.00330 (Iosevich-Pham-Senger-Tait VC-dimension refinement of Vinh, general-range). None states, implies, or computes an exact small-order projective-plane ceiling M(8,8)=24 in PG(2,4), an extremal degree type, or an attainer census; all operate asymptotically and are numerically far above 24 at (q=4,m=n=8). Internal prior scan corroborated: closest resultary hits SCOPE020 (caps in AG(3,3)/PG(3,3)) and SCOPE011 (quartic Cremona maps over F4) share finite-geometry language but concern different objects and no incidence ceiling; failed attempts SCOPE-FAIL-20260907-003 (Euclidean 4x4 Szemeredi-Trotter constant) and -023 (caps in PG(4,5)) differ in geometry, claim, and route. No source was found giving the (3^8)/(4,3^6,2) extremal classification or the 7560/7560/22680 census. A timestamp or failed search alone was not counted as priority; the comparison is substantive (exact bounded-order census vs general asymptotic upper bounds).

value.rationale: Independently worth finding later as a sharp small-order extremal lemma, not a textbook restatement. Not a formula plug-in: no cited general bound yields 24 (KST real 25.54/integer 25; spectral 31.24), and the integer 25-to-24 step requires the Cauchy/pair-disjointness reduction plus dual exhaustive certification, with a structural payoff (exactly two admissible sum-25 degree sequences; exactly two realized 24-pair types (3^8):2520 and (4,3^6,2):20160, point-line symmetric; full-21 profiles classified; neighboring sizes 7/9/10 certified 21/28/33). Not a tiny unmotivated gain: the 1-point gap over integer KST is accompanied by a 7-point gap over the spectral value, explicit extremal coordinates, per-side attainer counts, and a stated atlas/blocking-set/code motivation identifying PG(2,4) as the smallest plane where textbook analogues visibly overshoot. Not an unexplained enumeration: the count is explained by the KST integer ceiling, the degree-sequence classification, the top-k prefix-optimality principle (why 2xC(21,8) one-sided checks certify all pairs), dual symmetry, and replayable stdlib scripts running in seconds. Consistent with the passing precedent for small-geometry certified censuses (e.g. AG(3,3)/PG(3,3) caps); unlike rejected bare single-number SAT enumerations, this delivers types, witnesses, and a reusable bounded-regime template.
